our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a broad assessment of provider economics and customer outcomes, retaining the uncertainty expressed by 'seem' and 'appears'.
The financial comparison uses calendar 2025, the latest completed annual reporting period before the post. This is an evaluator choice because no common industry reporting period is supplied.
Productivity means measured output relative to labor or other inputs, with quality accounted for. Customer financial benefit means returns after adoption and operating costs.
Provider profitability, customer productivity, and customer net returns are separate questions. Evidence for one does not establish the others.
A single successful or unsuccessful deployment does not settle the broad assessment.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable industry financial evidence shows substantial net losses, and representative customer evidence shows no material productivity gains and negative net financial returns during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes broad provider profitability or substantial, repeatable customer productivity and net financial gains inconsistent with the asserted general pattern.
